Rashi on Temurah 11a:10:1.hebrew: אי אתה מוצא - שיהו הן קדושים, דלאיצטריך למיתני לא מקדישין, אלא במקדיש בהמה, ואח"כ נטרפה זו, והאי קדושה היא, דקדם הקדשה את מומה:
Rashi on Temurah 11a:10:1.english: You do not find - that these [animals] are sacred, [such that it would be necessary] to teach "they do not sanctify," except where one consecrated an animal and afterward this one became a tereifa. And this is [a case of] sanctity, because its consecration preceded its blemish:

Rashi on Temurah 11a:10:2.hebrew: במקדיש ולד - שהקדישו במעי אמו, דחיילה עליה קדושה מיד, והדר יצא דרך דופן:
Rashi on Temurah 11a:10:2.english: Where one consecrates an offspring - [i.e., where he consecrated it] in its mother's womb, for sanctity takes effect upon it immediately, and afterward it emerged through the side [by caesarean section]:

Rashi on Temurah 11a:11:1.hebrew: הני איצטריך למימר דאין מקדישין, וסיפא דמילתא מפרש בפרק יש בקרבנות (לקמן תמורה דף יז.):
Rashi on Temurah 11a:11:1.english: These — it was necessary to say that one does not consecrate [a blemished animal with inherent sanctity]; and the end of the matter is explained in the chapter "Yesh Bekorbanot" (below, Temurah 17a):

Rashi on Temurah 11a:12:1.hebrew: כלאים וטומטום ואנדרוגינוס אי אתה מוצא אלא בולדי קדשים - שנתעברה מהן בהמת קדשים לאחר הקדשה. אלמא קדיש עובר, מדקתני במקדיש עובר ויוצא דרך דופן. דהאי הוא דלא קדיש לגופיה למעבד תמורה, הא לא יצא דרך דופן — קדיש בקדושה קמייתא, קדושת הגוף, ועביד תמורה. וליכא לתרוצי קדושת דמים, דאי קדושת דמים לא הוה עביד תמורה אפילו יצא דרך רחם:
Rashi on Temurah 11a:12:1.english: Diverse kinds, a tumtum, and a hermaphrodite, you find only among the offspring of sacrificial animals - [This refers to a case] where a sacrificial animal became pregnant by them [i.e., by a different species, or with a tumtum or hermaphrodite] after it was consecrated. Evidently, the fetus is consecrated, since [the Mishnah] teaches the case of one who consecrates a fetus and it emerges through the side [by caesarean section]. For it is this [offspring] that is not consecrated in itself so as to effect substitution; but [one] that did not emerge through the side is consecrated with the first sanctity, the sanctity of the body, and effects substitution. And one cannot answer that it is the sanctity of monetary value, for if it were the sanctity of monetary value, it would not effect substitution even if it emerged through the womb.

Rashi on Temurah 11a:1:1.hebrew: הכי קאמר מקדישין איברין וממירין בהן כו' - כלומר, מקדישין אבר אחד, וממירין אחרי כן באותה בהמה. ואשמעינן האי "וממירין בהן", דהאי דקאמר "מקדישין אברין" לאו למקדיש אבר לחודיה, אלא למיפשט קדושה בכולה בהמה. דאי אאבר לחודיה, לא מצי למימר "וממירין בהן", דהא אפילו רבי יוסי דאמר ממירין אברין בשלמים, מודה דאין ממירין שלימין בהן, וכל שכן אברין באברין. ודקתני סיפא דהך ברייתא בפ' ב' "אבל לא ממירין", אשמעינן דאין ממירין בשלימים, דאם אמר "אבר בהמה זו תמורה", לא אקדשיה. והיינו חומר בתחילת הקדש מבתמורה: דתחילת הקדש, כי אקדיש חד אבר, פשט בכולה; ובתמורה, כי אמר "אבר זה תמורה תחת שלימה זו", לא קדשה:
Rashi on Temurah 11a:1:1.english: This is what it says: One consecrates limbs and substitutes with them, etc. - That is to say, one consecrates one limb, and afterward substitutes [for] that animal. And this phrase "and they substitute with them" teaches us that when it says "one consecrates limbs," it does not mean one who consecrates a limb alone, but rather that the sanctity spreads through the entire animal. For if [it were speaking] of a limb alone, it could not say "and they substitute with them," since even Rabbi Yosei, who says that one may substitute limbs [for] peace-offerings, agrees that one does not substitute whole [animals] for them, and certainly [not] limbs for limbs. And as for what the latter clause of this baraita in the second chapter teaches, "but one does not substitute," it teaches us that one does not substitute for whole [animals]: if one said, "A limb of this animal is its substitute," it is not consecrated. And this is the greater stringency in the initial act of consecration than in substitution: for in initial consecration, when one consecrates one limb, [the sanctity] spreads through the whole [animal]; but in substitution, when one says, "This limb is a substitute for this whole [animal]," it is not consecrated.

Rashi on Temurah 11a:1:2.hebrew: ועוברין שקדשו במעי אמן - כגון ולד קדשים, אע"פ שהן קדושין, אין ממירין בהמה בהן כל זמן שהן במעי אמן. והא לאו משום חומר בקדשים מבתמורה קתני, אלא משום דתנא "וממירין בהן" בבהמה שקדשה ע"י אבר, תני בעוברין "אין ממירין בהן". ור' יהודה היא [דאמר] ולד עושה תמורה, דאי רבנן — אבראי נמי לא עביד תמורה:
Rashi on Temurah 11a:1:2.english: And fetuses that were consecrated in their mother's womb - For example, the offspring of consecrated animals: even though they are sanctified, one does not substitute an animal for them as long as they are in their mother's womb. And the mishna does not teach this because of a greater stringency of consecrated items relative to substitution; rather, since it taught "and one substitutes for them" regarding an animal that was consecrated through a limb, it taught regarding fetuses "one does not substitute for them." And this is [in accordance with] Rabbi Yehuda, who says that an offspring effects substitution, for if it were the Rabbis — even outside [the womb] it does not effect substitution.

Rashi on Temurah 11a:5:1.hebrew: אלא לזכרי כהונה - כדין חטאת. קא סלקא דעתך דבמפריש בהמה מעוברת עסקינן, דאי במפריש ריקנית ונתעברה — דכולי עלמא הואיל ומכח אימיה הוא דקדיש, חולין הוא. דוולדי קדשים בהווייתן הן קדושים, כשהן נולדין, ולא במעי אמן:
Rashi on Temurah 11a:5:1.english: Only by the males of the priesthood - As is the law of a sin offering. It enters your mind that we are dealing with one who designates a pregnant animal, for if it were one who designates an empty one [that is, not pregnant] and it later became pregnant — everyone [agrees] that since [the fetus] is sanctified only by virtue of its mother, it is non-sacred. For the offspring of consecrated animals are sanctified at their [own] coming into being, when they are born, and not in their mother's womb:

Rashi on Temurah 11a:6:1.hebrew: מאי לאו תנאי היא - דלתנא קמא קדושה חלה על האברין מכח עצמן, כשהיא מעוברת בשעת הקדש קדיש לאלתר, דלא כוולדי קדשים הוא; ולתנא בתרא אין קדושה חלה עליו אלא מכח אמו, וכשאר ולדי קדשים הוא, דבהווייתן הוא דקדישי. ולהכי נקט חי — רבותא קא משמע לן: דלא אמרי' הואיל וחי הוא, הווייתו חשיב ליה, ואפילו לתנא בתרא ליקדש מכח אמו כשאר ולדי קדשים — קא משמע לן דהואיל ולא כלו חדשיו, לאו הווייתו הוא:
Rashi on Temurah 11a:6:1.english: Is it not a dispute between tanna'im? - According to the first tanna, sanctity takes effect on the limbs [of the fetus] by its own force: when [the mother] is pregnant at the time of the consecration, [the fetus] is sanctified immediately, for it is not like the offspring of consecrated animals. But according to the later tanna, sanctity takes effect on it only through its mother, and it is like other offspring of consecrated animals, which are sanctified only at their birth. And therefore [the baraita] mentioned a live [fetus] — it is teaching us a novelty: we do not say, "Since it is alive, its birth is considered to have occurred," so that even according to the later tanna it should be sanctified through its mother like other offspring of consecrated animals. It teaches us that since its months were not completed, this is not its [proper] birth.

Rashi on Temurah 11a:7:1.hebrew: לא - במפריש בהמה מעוברת לא איירי הכא כלל, אלא בבהמת קדשים שנתעברה. ובהא פליגי: תנא קמא סבר ולדות קדשים בהוייתן הן קדושין — כשהן נולדין הן קדושין, ולא במעי אמן:
Rashi on Temurah 11a:7:1.english: No - [The baraita] is not dealing here at all with one who sets aside a pregnant animal, but rather with an animal of sacrificial status that became pregnant. And in this they disagree: the first Tanna holds that the offspring of sacrificial animals are sanctified only upon their coming into being — that is, they are sanctified when they are born, and not in their mothers' wombs:

Rashi on Temurah 11a:7:2.hebrew: בהווייתן - לישנא דקרא נקט, דאיתרבו ולדות מיניה, דכתיב (דברים י״ב:כ״ו) "רק קדשיך אשר יהיו לך" וגו', ואמר מר: "אשר יהיו לך" — אלו הוולדות, בפרק שני דבכורות (דף יד:):
Rashi on Temurah 11a:7:2.english: When they come into being - [The Gemara] used the language of the verse, from which offspring are included, as it is written (Deuteronomy 12:26): "Only your sacred things that you have [yihyu lekha]…" And the Master said: "That you will have [asher yihyu lekha]" — these are the offspring, in the second chapter of Bekhorot (14b).

Rashi on Temurah 11a:8:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא חד תנא הוא - הנך תרתי מתנייתא, ודכולי עלמא קדושה חלה על העוברין לאלתר, כר' יוחנן. והך דקתני דלא קדיש עובר, במקדיש בהמה ואח"כ נתעברה — דוולדות קדשים בהווייתן הן קדושין. והאי דקתני דקדיש ולד לאלתר ולא הוי כשאר ולדי קדשים — היינו דעובר לאו ירך אמו, כשהקדישה מעוברת:
Rashi on Temurah 11a:8:1.english: And if you wish, say: it is one tanna - These two baraitot [are by one tanna], and everyone agrees that sanctity takes effect on fetuses immediately, like Rabbi Yoḥanan. And that [baraita] which teaches that the fetus is not sanctified [applies] where one consecrates an animal and afterward it became pregnant, since the offspring of consecrated animals are sanctified [only] at their birth. And that [baraita] which teaches that the offspring is sanctified immediately, and is not like other offspring of consecrated animals, [is] because a fetus is not the thigh of its mother, [and applies] where he consecrated it while it was pregnant.

Rashi on Temurah 11a:9:1.hebrew: לא קדושין בתמורה - שאם הן חולין והמירן בבהמת קדשים, אינם נתפסין. ואפילו תמורה שחלה על בעלי מומין קבועין, אינה חלה עליהן. וכל שכן אם הקדישם ממש, שהן אינן קדושין:
Rashi on Temurah 11a:9:1.english: Not sacred as a substitute - For if they are non-sacred and one exchanged them for a sacrificial animal, the sanctity does not take hold of them. Even substitution, which takes effect on animals with permanent blemishes, does not take effect on them. And all the more so, if one actually consecrated them, they are not sacred.

Rashi on Temurah 11a:9:2.hebrew: ואין מקדישין - אחר לעשותו תמורה. אם הן קדושין והמיר בהמת חולין בהן, ורבי מאיר מפרש: היכי משכחת לה דליהוי קדושין? מאחר שהן אינן קדושין בשום קדושת הגוף, מהיכן יהו הן מקדישין ועושין תמורה? והא עץ בעלמא נינהו:
Rashi on Temurah 11a:9:2.english: And they do not sanctify - another animal to make it a substitute, if these are sacred and one exchanged a non-sacred animal for them. And Rabbi Meir explains: How can you find a case where they would be sacred? Since they are not sacred with any sanctity of the body, from where could they sanctify and create a substitute? Aren't they merely wood?

Tosafot on Temurah 11a:5:1.hebrew: השוחט את החטאת - כגון שעירה, דאילו כשבה אי אפשר לילד תוך שנתה, כדאיתא בבכורות (דף יט:):
Tosafot on Temurah 11a:5:1.english: If one slaughtered a sin offering - For example, a female goat; for a female lamb cannot give birth within its first year, as stated in Bekhorot (19b):

Tosafot on Temurah 11a:5:2.hebrew: ומצא בה בן ארבע חי - דאילו בן ה' בבהמה דקה אינה ניתרת לרבנן בשחיטת אמו, כמבואר פרק בהמה המקשה (חולין דף עד.):
Tosafot on Temurah 11a:5:2.english: "And he found in it a living four-month-old" - For if it were a five-month-old in a small animal, it would not be permitted by the slaughter of its mother, according to the Rabbis, as explained in the chapter Behemah HaMekashah (Chullin 74a):
